data.body: rebar-debug Phase 1 RCA — completion close failure. Problem: the normal close verifier returned FAIL for 10 criteria after the primary aggregate run hit its 150-request runaway guard and bounded recovery completed. Proven root cause: those 10 checkbox lines omit the exact `[operator-attested]` prefix, so ADR-0043 and the completion-verifier prompt classify them as codebase-verifiable and deliberately refuse to accept ticket-comment evidence. The rejected proof lives in command execution, git history, CI/Gerrit/PyPI, or the external Homebrew tap; the final receipts comment contains concrete outputs, URLs, timestamps, commit ids, and hashes, but comments can satisfy only correctly tagged operator-attested criteria. Proof: the live finalizer named the missing tag in every failure; `.rebar/usage.jsonl` shows all bounded evidence calls and the tool-free finalizer completed successfully, proving the origin/main recovery fix is active rather than crashing; ADR-0043 §Decision and `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md` §Criterion kinds specify the exact fail-safe classification. A deterministic experiment against `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` returned `[]` for all 10 exact lines, explaining why plan review supplied no evidence-kind coaching; that detector gap is separate follow-up risk, not the cause of this validator verdict. Classification: intended validator behavior / ticket-contract mismatch. Remediation: prefix the 10 runtime/external criteria with `[operator-attested]`, retain the existing concrete receipts, refresh the now-stale plan review, and retry normal close without force. A tagged retry will also discriminate the remaining low-confidence recovery-locality hypothesis: if recovery still rejects the receipts, return to Phase 1 on the recovery prompts.
